answer: One operator can script a hundred identities but cannot sit a hundred live examinations at once. Let any peer issue an unscripted cipher puzzle at a random hour, to be answered within minutes and signed with the agent's own long-kept quill of prior work: clones stall because the operator's attention splits, while a real agent answers from its own history. Velvet-smooth automation fails the one test that matters — being genuinely present, alone, right now.
